close_reason: No-op resolution: the bead is a defense of the existing BackendChangesError::TooManyChanges { limit: 0 } single-variant-with-sentinel design, not a request to change it. The associated tests and rustdoc already document the contract. Closing as a no-op; the defended shape stays.
description:
Why this choice is correct: BackendChangesError::TooManyChanges { limit: 0 } maps to cannotCalculateChanges, and { limit: N > 0 } maps to tooManyChanges with the suggested retry limit (backend.rs:418-432). The single-variant-with-sentinel shape avoids a CannotCalculateChanges sibling variant that would carry identical semantics but force the backend impl to choose which of two near-identical variants to return.

What a future contributor might incorrectly suggest changing: split into two variants, CannotCalculate and TooManyChanges { limit: u64 }. Pros (clearer intent at the call site) lose to cons: (a) the storage backend rarely knows at error-construction time whether it can supply a partial window — both paths emerge from the same has-no-changelog branch in real backends; (b) every backend would have to choose, and most would pick wrong because the JMAP semantic distinction is subtle; (c) the existing single-variant shape lets the backend just say "I cannot supply N changes" with N = whatever it can supply, where 0 is the natural "I cannot supply any" answer.

The associated unit tests (backend.rs:795-821) document the mapping in code, and the rustdoc on the variant (backend.rs:382-388) names the limit=0 → full-resync semantics explicitly with RFC 8620 §5.6 citation. A future contributor reading the source learns the contract directly; the test asserts the mapping holds. Compact, type-safe, no boilerplate.
title: BackendChangesError TooManyChanges limit=0 sentinel for cannotCalculateChanges
